decisions.reason: A classic lever handle line close to the core offer fits the established business at low marginal cost, and with industry turnover growing there is no shortfall against aspiration to trigger problemistic search.
This multi-model handle family extends the core range that architects specify, and the firm's slack in a growing market lets it keep the line while it builds adoption.
A single handle design is cheap to carry within a broad range, and one year is too early to judge it below aspiration, though single designs are more easily rationalized later.
Like C, this is a low-cost design addition close to the core, with no evidence of underperformance that would justify withdrawal so soon after launch.
A lever handle family with several models supports the firm's system-breadth strategy, and stable industry growth leaves performance near aspiration.
The flagship electronic access system embodies the strategic move toward digital building organization, so slack and strategic commitment justify carrying it even while results are uncertain.
